production.note: US model years, from Kelley Blue Book (a database): KBB's 2021 Huracán lists "STO Coupe 2D" ("The range-topping 2021 Huracan STO Coupe 2D"), and its 2024 Huracán lists "STO Coupe 2D" (kbb-huracan-2024), whose year selector ends at 2024. Motor1 (motor1-huracan-sto): customer deliveries from spring 2021, US price $327,838. Evo dates the car 2021-2023 (UK).

configuration.note: Evo panel: "Engine | V10, 5204cc". Lamborghini (lambo-huracan-sto-page): "5.2-liter V10 naturally aspirated engine".

drivetrain.note: Evo: rear-wheel drive only, with "the front driveshafts removed". Motor1 (motor1-huracan-sto): rear-wheel-drive layout.

transmission.note: Evo: "The engine and 7-speed DCT 'box remain absolutely sublime." (Lamborghini LDF dual-clutch.) No manual offered.

powerHp.note: Quote (Lamborghini model page): "Max. power: 470/640 at 8,000 rpm" (kW/CV). 640 CV x 0.98632 = 631 hp. Evo spec panel (evo-huracan-sto): "Power | 631bhp @ 8000rpm". No separate US SAE rating was found, so powerStandard is DIN PS, as in the other Huracán records. Motor1's "630 horsepower (470 kilowatts)" is a rounded US conversion of the same rating.

weightLb.note: DRY weight (guide step 4). Quote (Evo spec panel, review by Jethro Bovingdon, Stuart Gallagher and John Barker): "Weight | 1339kg (dry)"; text: "a dry weight of 1339kg… some 43kg lighter than the Performante". 1,339 x 2.20462 = 2,952 lb. Motor1 (motor1-huracan-sto, reproducing the launch figures): "dry weight of 1,339 kg (2,951 lbs)". No curb weight for the standard car (step 1 or 2) and no optioned-car curb weight (step 3) was found from Lamborghini or a major magazine; Lamborghini's model page gives no weight. No opened page says whether the dry figure assumes options. A car with fluids is heavier.
